items.followUp: Define dipole-dipole forces and give one example.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding involves an attraction associated with hydrogen bonded to a highly electronegative atom.
rubric.description: Defines the attraction involved in hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the attraction involving hydrogen and a highly electronegative atom.

rubric.why: Water, HF and ammonia are examples of substances that exhibit hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding is the attraction between a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom and a highly electronegative atom of another molecule.
For example, hydrogen bonding occurs between water molecules (H₂O).

items.followUp: Why is distilled water a poor conductor of electricity?

rubric.why: Acetic acid ionizes only partially in water and therefore produces few ions.
rubric.description: Explains why CH₃COOH is a weak electrolyte.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acetic acid ionizes partially or produces few ions in water.

rubric.why: Calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble in water, so its solution contains relatively few ions.
rubric.description: Explains why Ca(OH)₂ is considered a weak electrolyte in this context.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble or that its solution contains relatively few ions.

modelAnswer: Acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is a weak electrolyte because it ionizes only partially in water and produces few ions.
Calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)₂] is sparingly soluble in water, so its solution contains relatively few ions and conducts electricity weakly.

items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of magnesium much greater than the second?

rubric.why: The second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion formed after the first ionization.
rubric.description: Identifies the ion from which the second electron is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the second electron is removed from Mg⁺.

rubric.why: The remaining electron is held more strongly by the positive ion, so more energy is needed to remove it.
rubric.description: Explains why the second ionization energy is greater.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the stronger attraction to the greater energy needed.

modelAnswer: After the first electron is removed, the second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion.
Mg⁺ attracts its remaining electrons more strongly than neutral Mg does, so more energy is required to remove the second electron.
